issues.description: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None; caller splices literal 'None' into the synthesized URL
issues.detail: extract_arch_from_url returns Optional[str] but use_koji_url_only treats the result as str, producing '.../latest/None/Packages/...' when the regex misses. There is no check, no log, no raise — the broken URL is written into rpms.lock.yaml and surfaces as a confusing 404 at fetch time. Either tighten the helper's contract to raise on miss, or have the caller handle None explicitly. Better: thread the arch in from generate_main (which already knows it per-iteration) and delete the regex extraction entirely.

issues.description: nevra[0] indexes the RPM filename, not the package name; assumption is unstated and brittle
issues.detail: nevra = url.split('/')[-1] yields a filename like 'foo-1.2-3.fc40.x86_64.rpm' — not a NEVRA — and nevra[0].lower() takes the first character of that filename to build the koji '/Packages/<letter>/' shard. This works for ordinary ASCII-letter names by accident, but breaks for digit-prefixed names (389-ds-base, 3proxy, 7zip), empty trailing segments (URL ending in '/'), and URLs with query strings or fragments. Parse the filename into a structured value (name, version, release, arch), derive the bucket letter from the package name, and validate the input ends in '.rpm'.

issues.description: Whole-URL regex for arch can match the wrong token; arch should come from a known structural position
issues.detail: The regex scans the entire URL for any arch substring with word boundaries and returns the first match. Nothing guarantees the first match is the package arch — a mirror path, a koji tag name, a username, or a future hostname containing 'x86_64' would silently win. The arch lives in a known position: either the caller's loop variable in generate_main, or the '.arch.rpm' suffix of the filename. Read it from the structured position you trust, not by scanning the string.

issues.description: Supported arch list is hardcoded and duplicated across the codebase
issues.detail: ['x86_64', 'aarch64', 'ppc64le', 's390x'] is inlined in extract_arch_from_url while generate_main iterates arches separately and cosalib.cmdlib already exposes get_basearch. Lift the arch set to a single module-level constant (or reuse the shared one) so adding a new arch is a one-place edit rather than a silent-failure waiting to be forgotten.

issues.description: 'coreos-pool' substring check is too loose; should be a prefix match against koji_url_base
issues.detail: Both the new use_koji_url_only and the pre-existing prioritization in query_packages_location decide 'is this already a coreos-pool URL?' via substring containment of the literal 'coreos-pool'. That admits any URL with the string anywhere — a path component named 'not-coreos-pool-mirror', a query string, a future hostname. Tighten to url.startswith(koji_url_base) so the 'pass-through' and 'rewrite' branches are genuinely disjoint, and consolidate the literal into one module-level constant.

issues.description: No unit tests for two pure string-transforming functions
issues.detail: use_koji_url_only and extract_arch_from_url are pure functions over URL strings — trivially testable without any koji round-trip. The PR description concedes rpms.lock.yaml changes cannot be tested locally end-to-end, but that does not preclude unit coverage for: coreos-pool passthrough, fedora-secondary rewrites for ppc64le/s390x, digit-prefixed package names (389-ds-base), URLs with no recognized arch (should raise), and URLs where 'x86_64' appears elsewhere in the path. Tests here would have caught the nevra[0] and None-arch defects.

issues.description: Race condition with coreos-koji-tagger is acknowledged in commit message but unguarded and unmentioned in code
issues.detail: The author flags two real properties: a race between bump-lockfile merge and coreos-koji-tagger tagging, and inability to test rpms.lock.yaml locally. These are time-semantics facts about when the synthesized URLs become valid. Neither is encoded in the code — no docstring at use_koji_url_only naming 'URLs produced here are predicted and only valid after coreos-koji-tagger tags the NEVRA', no log of which URLs were synthesized vs passed through, no HEAD-check or retry. At minimum a docstring/comment at the call site would breadcrumb future maintainers debugging a flaky hermetic build.

issues.description: coreos-pool prioritization in query_packages_location is now redundant with the downstream rewrite
issues.detail: query_packages_location still prefers coreos-pool URLs when multiple repos return the same NEVRA, but generate_main now rewrites every non-coreos-pool URL into a coreos-pool URL anyway. Two overlapping policies for the same property leave the next reader guessing which layer owns the rule. Pick one: if the rewrite is the policy, delete the prioritization; if the prioritization is a load-bearing fast path, comment why both exist.

issues.description: Regex compiled per-call and overkill for a path-segment match
issues.detail: extract_arch_from_url recompiles the same regex on every URL inside a loop, and a URL is already '/'-delimited — splitting on '/' and checking set membership against the arch constant is shorter, regex-escape-free, and makes the data shape (path segments) explicit. Minor on its own, but combined with the duplicated arch list and the wrong-match risk above, lifting the arch set to a constant and switching to segment membership makes the regex disappear.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch is a reasonable workaround for a real DNF5 bug, scoped well, and shaped correctly as a stateless URL-list transform — but the new helpers carry unstated contracts and at least two silent failure modes that should block merge in their current form. extract_arch_from_url returns Optional[str] while the caller treats it as str, so a non-matching URL produces '.../latest/None/Packages/...' written into rpms.lock.yaml. nevra is actually a filename indexed at [0] for a koji shard letter, which breaks for digit-prefixed package names and any URL not ending in a bare .rpm. The arch should be threaded in from generate_main (which already knows it) rather than scanned out of the URL string with a regex that can match the wrong token. Add fail-loud validation, unit tests for these pure functions, a docstring naming the race against coreos-koji-tagger, and reconcile the now-redundant coreos-pool prioritization in query_packages_location with the downstream rewrite.
